Consequences confirmed: (a) with a client clock ahead of the server, the first tick after each clockSync subtracts skew + real elapsed, so the display drops by the skew and is restored by the next sync — and once the server-authoritative remaining time falls below the skew, `Math.max(0, ms - elapsed)` (clock.ts:109/117) hits 0, checkTimeUp fires, and the store sets gameStatus 'timeout'/gameResult/winner locally, popping GameOverDialog and locking the board (selectPiece/executeMove/handleSquareClick all early-return on 'timeout'); (b) with a client clock behind the server, `elapsed` is negative and the active clock counts UPWARD between syncs (Math.max does not clamp an increase); (c) even at zero skew, the client is a second clock authority that unilaterally declares the flag.

The real symptom is a per-second display jump equal to the skew plus a premature/false timeout once remaining time <= skew (immediate if skew exceeds remaining time). The defect itself stands; only the drift rate was overstated.

claim: The SAN disambiguation filter looks for same-type friendly pieces standing ON the mover's legal destination squares, which is impossible, so sameTypeMoves is always empty and the server never emits a disambiguator.

Not dead code and not unreachable: GameRoomManager.ts:202 deliberately snapshots the pre-move board (`cloneBoard`, with a comment saying generateSAN needs it for disambiguation) and passes it at line 213 while the mover is still on `from`; the resulting SAN goes through appendCheckStatus into `move.san` (line 283), into room.moveHistory (line 316), and out to clients. server/src/index.ts:146-148 wires the socket `makeMove` event to it. (The wrong piece letter — `piece.type[0].toUpperCase()` at line 36 gives 'K' for 'knight' — is a separate defect the reviewer already flagged separately; it is real too but I left it out of the fix below to keep this minimal.)

So its third parameter must be the MOVER's color. server/src/chess/board.ts:138 confirms `isInCheck(board, color)` = "is color's own king attacked" (`isSquareAttacked(board, findKing(board,color), oppositeColor)`) — there is no inverted-argument misreading available.

Any move surviving validation at GameRoomManager.ts:191-192 leaves the mover's king safe, so the predicate inside appendCheckStatus is unconditionally false and the '+'/'#' branch is dead code.

Every check-giving move of every online game gets a bare SAN, so the online move list and PGN export lack all check/mate markers, while local play via src/chess/san.ts:134 (which derives the color from `move.piece.color`) yields `Qxf7#`.

claim: `analyzeAllMoves` throws out of its loop and discards every review when any analysed position has no legal move, which is exactly the final position of any game that ended in checkmate or stalemate.
reasoning:
Confirmed from the code; I could not refute it.

Stockfish emits exactly `info depth 0 score mate 0` + `bestmove (none)` for a root position with no legal moves, so checkmate and stalemate positions take this branch.

2. useAnalysisStore.ts:464-603 iterates `for (let i = 0; i < moveHistory.length; i++)`. On the final iteration `fenAfter` (line 554) is generated from `newBoard` with `nextTurn` = the side that was just mated, i.e. a genuinely terminal FEN, and lines 555-556 unconditionally call `engine.setPosition(fenAfter)` then `await engine.go({...analysisConfig, depth: 15})`. There is no try/catch inside the loop body and no legal-move precheck; the only early exit is the cancellation `break` at 467, which does not fire because `isReviewing` is still true.

The rejection therefore escapes the loop to the single `catch (error)` at 609, so `set({ moveReviews: reviews })` at 605 never executes. `moveReviews` stays `[]` from the reset at 436, while `reviewProgress` was already advanced to N/N at line 472 — the user sees a 100%-complete sweep with zero reviews and only `console.error('Review error:', ...)`. Refutation attempts that failed:
- Reachability: AnalysisPage.tsx:160 wires the button to `analyzeAllMoves`, and `extractMoves` in src/chess/pgn.ts:98-121 keeps every SAN token (including the final `#` mating move), so a mate-terminated PGN yields a moveHistory whose last position is the mate. Games ending in checkmate/stalemate are ordinary input.
- The `if (!clickedPiece) continue;` at 506 does not skip the final iteration on a correctly replayed board, and a mated root returns immediately so the search timeout is irrelevant.
- No precedence or nullability misread: the throw happens before `evaluation`/`bestMove` are consumed, so the `EvaluationData | null` typing is not a mitigating factor.
- The service-level reject cannot simply be softened, because useChessStore.ts:928 (`engine.getBestMove(fen)`) also depends on that contract; the fix belongs in the analysis store.

The secondary part of the claim (analyzeCurrentPosition, line 390) is also accurate but far milder: that reject is caught at 398, so the user merely gets an empty eval/lines panel plus a console error when analysing a mated position rather than losing work.

claim: `analyzeCurrentPosition` and `analyzeAllMoves` guard on separate flags (`isAnalyzing` vs `isReviewing`) while sharing one singleton engine, so they can be driven concurrently and corrupt each other's position, options and score sign.

I could not refute this; every premise independently checks out in the code.

CONFIRMED PREMISES:
1. Separate, non-overlapping guards. useAnalysisStore.ts:372-373 destructures only `isAnalyzing` and returns on it. Line 433-434 destructures only `isReviewing` and returns on it (plus empty history). Neither reads the other's flag. Grep over src/ shows no third guard anywhere.
2. UI permits it. AnalysisPage.tsx:170 is `disabled={isAnalyzing}` — enabled during a review, since a review never sets `isAnalyzing`. AnalysisPage.tsx:160 is `disabled={isReviewing || moveHistory.length === 0}` — enabled during a position analysis, so the collision is bidirectional (the reviewer only claimed one direction).
3. Shared singleton. Both call `getEngineService()` (lines 378 and 439), which returns the module-level `engineInstance` (chessEngineService.ts:630-635). One worker, one `this.search`, one `this.sideToMove`.
4. Perspective is read per-info-line, not captured per-search. `setPosition` assigns `this.sideToMove` synchronously with no in-flight-search check (chessEngineService.ts:484-486). `parseInfo` reads `this.sideToMove` at line 413 each time a line arrives. `handleInfo` overwrites `search.lastEvaluation` on every scored line (line 357) and `handleBestMove` returns precisely that last value (line 402). So a mid-search flip does sign-invert the value the review consumes via `scoreToCentipawns` (useAnalysisStore.ts:486, 558), which flows into `evalChange` and the blunder/best classification at lines 566-582.
5. `setConfig` has no in-flight protection at all; it unconditionally posts `setoption name MultiPV value 3` (chessEngineService.ts:465, 474) during the review's `go`.
6. `go()` throws when `this.search` is non-null (chessEngineService.ts:504-506).
7. Loss of all accumulated work is real. If the review's `await engine.go(...)` (line 477 or 556) is the loser, the throw skips `set({ moveReviews: reviews })` at line 605 and lands in the catch at 609, so `moveReviews` remains the `[]` written at line 436 — the user watched the progress bar reach ~100% and gets nothing.

REACHABILITY: Both functions are `async` on the single main thread, and `ensureReady()` resolves ALL queued `readyWaiters` on one `readyok` (chessEngineService.ts:313-318), so a click landing while the review is parked at any await produces a true interleave. Both race outcomes are reachable: parked at `go` (line 477/556) -> the analysis `go` throws and is silently swallowed at line 399; parked at `setPosition` (line 476/555) -> the analysis `go` wins and the review's `go` throws, destroying the review.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (a) the loop's cancellation check at line 467 reads `get().isReviewing`, which `analyzeCurrentPosition` never modifies, so the review does not self-abort; (b) the engine does not serialise — only `go` throws, and `setPosition`/`setConfig` mutate shared state freely; (c) no guard exists in AnalysisPage, EngineEvaluation, or elsewhere.

ADDITIONAL FINDING (worse than claimed): `analyzeCurrentPosition`'s `engine.setPosition(fen)` at line 386 can post `position fen <displayed board>` in the window before the review's `go` command reaches the worker, in which case the review's search evaluates an entirely unrelated position, not merely a sign-flipped one.

claim: goToMove rewinds board/currentTurn/castlingRights/halfmoveClock in the live game store without freezing play or truncating moveHistory/positionHistory, so a move played from a rewound position is appended to the full history.

Make analysisIndex authoritative for "am I at the tip of the game" and refuse moves when rewound, in the store (Square.tsx's drag-drop calls executeMove directly, so a component guard is insufficient).

```ts
    // Board navigation rewinds the live position without truncating history,
    // so moves may only be played from the tip of the game.
    const { analysisIndex, moveHistory } = get();
    if (analysisIndex !== moveHistory.length) return false;
```

2. Keep analysisIndex in sync with the tip everywhere moveHistory changes, so the guard is a no-op in normal play:

Optional but advisable: bail out early in makeEngineMove (~line 911) with the same tip check so the engine does not burn a search whose executeMove will be rejected, and have GamePage snap back with goToMove(moveHistory.length) before allowing input (or disable the board visually while analysisIndex !== moveHistory.length) so the rejected click is not silent.

Reachability is confirmed and is in fact broader than the report:
- GamePage.tsx:95-116 gates ArrowLeft/ArrowRight on `gameStatus !== 'playing' || moveHistory.length > 0`, which is true during live play with moves, and Home/End are ungated. So rewinding mid-game is a single keypress.
- src\components\chess\Square.tsx handleDrop calls executeMove DIRECTLY with no gameStatus/analysisIndex guard, bypassing ChessBoard's `isGameOver = gameStatus !== 'playing'` check (ChessBoard.tsx:51-59). So the fix cannot live in a component; it must be in the store.

- Computer mode corrupts with no user move at all when the human plays black: after the rewind currentTurn flips back to 'white' === computerColor, so the GamePage.tsx:73-82 effect re-fires and makeEngineMove -> executeMove appends to the full history.

One detail in the report is wrong but does not rescue the code: analysisIndex is never advanced by executeMove (it stays 0 through live play; only goToMove writes it, and newGame/loadFEN never reset it). So the first ArrowLeft computes `idx = 0` and calls goToMove(0), rewinding to the start position - strictly more destructive than the described goToMove(1). The reviewer's exact state is reached with ArrowRight instead (analysisIndex 0 < moveHistory.length 2 -> goToMove(1), board after 1.e4, currentTurn 'black'), after which playing 1...c5 gives moveHistory [e4, e5, c5] on a board matching [e4, c5], and positionHistory gains a key from the spliced line so threefold/50-move detection runs over an impossible game.

claim: Analysis and move review run the engine with `UCI_LimitStrength: true` / `UCI_Elo: 1600` / `Skill Level: 10` inherited from `getDifficultyEngineConfig('medium')`, so the "best move" the review reports is a deliberately randomised handicapped move rather than the engine's actual best.
reasoning: Confirmed; I could not refute it. initialState.engineConfig = getDifficultyEngineConfig('medium') (useAnalysisStore.ts:142) really does carry skillLevel: 10, uciElo: 1600, uciLimitStrength: true (chessEngineService.ts:56-64, 89-100). Both analyzeCurrentPosition (line 381) and analyzeAllMoves (line 442) spread it straight into analysisConfig and hand it to engine.setConfig, which at chessEngineService.ts:467-471 unconditionally posts `setoption name UCI_LimitStrength value true`, `UCI_Elo 1600` and `Skill Level 10` (the `!== undefined` guards pass because the values are genuinely present, and multi-word/boolean setoption syntax is valid UCI). Stockfish builds its handicap as Skill(options["Skill Level"], UCI_LimitStrength ? UCI_Elo : 0); Elo 1600 maps to a level of roughly 1.7, so skill.enabled() is true, internal MultiPV is forced to >= 4, and the emitted `bestmove` comes from Skill::pick_best, which adds an RNG term (weakness ~117) to the top-4 root scores and returns the argmax. So the returned bestmove is a deliberately weakened, run-to-run nondeterministic pick, and that is exactly the value consumed at lines 483-484 (evalBeforeResult.bestMove, i.e. the parsed `bestmove` line at chessEngineService.ts:385-386, not lines[0].bestMove) and stored as bestMove/bestMoveSan. No guard exists anywhere: setEngineConfig has zero callers in src/, setDifficulty only swaps in another preset, and every entry in DIFFICULTY_LEVELS sets uciLimitStrength: true. The path is one click away and user-visible: AnalysisPage.tsx:160 wires "Review All Moves" to analyzeAllMoves and lines 250-254 render `Best: {bestMoveSan}`; AnalysisPage.tsx:170 wires "Analyze Position" to analyzeCurrentPosition. Additionally (understated by the reviewer), the forced internal MultiPV >= 4 makes Stockfish emit info lines for multipv 1..4 per depth, and search.lastEvaluation (chessEngineService.ts:357) retains the last one seen, so evalBefore/evalAfter (lines 486/558) are often the 4th-best line's score, further skewing the classification thresholds at lines 572-582. The fix is safe for gameplay because useChessStore.ts:920 re-posts its own difficulty config before every engine move.

claim: resign() (and offerDraw() at line 428) require gameStatus === 'playing', so neither works while the player is in check.
fix:
Use the existing helper for the live-state checks in server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts:

- Line 428 (offerDraw): replace
    if (room.gameStatus !== 'playing') return { success: false, error: 'Game not in progress' };
  with
    if (!isLiveStatus(room.gameStatus)) return { success: false, error: 'Game not in progress' };

- Line 473 (resign): identical replacement.

isLiveStatus already excludes 'idle', so resigning before an opponent joins stays blocked, and no call sites or exported names change. Optionally apply the same change at line 389 (handleTimeUp), which has the same defect — flagging while in check currently returns null and the flag is never processed.
reasoning:
Confirmed from the code. GameStatus includes 'check' (server/src/chess/types.ts:4) and makeMove assigns room.gameStatus = 'check' whenever a move delivers check (GameRoomManager.ts:307-308), for the side to move. resign() (line 473) and offerDraw() (line 428) gate on `room.gameStatus !== 'playing'`, so both return {success:false,error:'Game not in progress'} in that state, while the file's own isLiveStatus helper (lines 33-39) documents the opposite contract ("a player can move, flag, resign or offer a draw. 'check' is just as live as 'playing'") and is used at makeMove:185 and getRunningGameIds:172. index.ts:222-229 calls resign() directly and emits 'gameEnded'/'gameState' only inside `if (result.success && result.game)`, so nothing is broadcast and the room never terminates.

I tried four refutations and all failed. (1) 'check' is a real GameStatus member. (2) index.ts has no compensating guard or status normalisation. (3) 'check' is visible to both sockets, so neither player can resign or offer a draw. (4) The strongest refutation — BoardControls.tsx:38 sets isGameOver = gameStatus !== 'playing' && gameStatus !== 'idle', which hides the Resign/Offer-Draw buttons during 'check' — does not make it unreachable, because the resign confirmation dialog at BoardControls.tsx:251 renders outside the !isGameFinished block. Concrete reachable path: while status is 'playing' the player clicks Resign and the dialog opens; the opponent's checking move lands and the server flips to 'check'; the button unmounts but the open dialog survives; the player clicks Resign in the dialog -> confirmResign -> resignOnlineGame -> multiplayerService.callWithCallback (lines 191-204) rejects on success:false, so the await throws, setShowResignConfirm(false) never runs, no 'gameEnded' is emitted, and the game hangs with only an unhandled promise rejection. Same for offering a draw.

One detail in the claim is wrong but immaterial: handleTimeUp at line 389 also uses `!== 'playing'`, so not every other live-state test goes through isLiveStatus — flagging while in check is broken too, which is a third instance of the same defect rather than a counterexample.

claim: `search.lastEvaluation` (and `this.currentEvaluation` / `lastInfoRaw`) is overwritten by every scored `info` line regardless of its `multipv` index, so for a MultiPV search the reported `EngineMove.evaluation` is the LAST-printed variation (multipv N, the worst line), not the best one.
reasoning:
Confirmed, and I could not construct a refutation.

1. chessEngineService.ts:351-357 assigns `this.currentEvaluation`, fires `onEvaluationCallback`, and sets `search.lastInfoRaw`/`search.lastEvaluation` before `const multipv = info.multipv ?? 1` is even computed (line 359). The multipv index is used only to key the `search.lines` map; the sole guard present (`!existing || existing.depth <= info.depth`, line 364) protects `lines`, not `lastEvaluation`. So every scored `info` line overwrites the final evaluation.

2. handleBestMove (line 395-403) returns `lines` sorted ascending by multipv (so `lines[0]` is genuinely the best line) but `evaluation: search.lastEvaluation`, i.e. whatever the last-printed info line was. The two fields are therefore sourced from different variations.

3. Print order: Stockfish's SearchManager::pv() iterates `for (i = 0; i < multiPV; ++i)` emitting one `info ... multipv i+1` per iteration via onUpdateFull, so each depth's PV block is ascending and the final scored info before `bestmove` is the highest multipv index (the worst of the reported lines). Nothing in the app reorders before the assignment.

4. Reachability with stock defaults: useAnalysisStore.ts:146 `multiPV: 3`; line 381 spreads it into `analysisConfig`; setConfig posts `setoption name MultiPV value 3` (line 465); line 395 stores `currentEvaluation: result.evaluation`. AnalysisPage.tsx:196-211 passes it to EvaluationBar (drives bar height and the printed number via `formatEvaluation(score, mate)`) and to EngineEvaluation, whose headline `evalText` comes from `evalData` while `bestMove` comes from `lines[0]?.bestMove` (EngineEvaluation.tsx:36-45) — exactly the described inconsistency. useSettingsStore.ts:91-92 default both `showEvaluationBar` and `showEngineEvaluation` to true, and the Analyze Position button is enabled unless a search is in flight. One click reproduces it.

5. The strongest available refutation fails: older Stockfish `UCI::pv()` returned all N lines as one newline-joined string, which the app's single-line parser would have collapsed to `multipv 1` (making the eval accidentally correct). That is not the case here — public/stockfish/stockfish-18-single.js uses `listener: function(e){ postMessage(e) }`, i.e. one postMessage per sync_endl flush, and SF 18 calls onUpdateFull once per multipv line, so lines arrive individually.

Aggravating factors (not required for the finding): every difficulty preset sets `uciLimitStrength: true`, and Stockfish forces MultiPV to at least 4 when strength limiting / Skill Level is active, so the surviving line is usually multipv 4 rather than 3. Also, because the engine is a singleton and `getDifficultyEngineConfig` never sends `multiPV`, the elevated MultiPV persists into useChessStore.makeEngineMove's `onEvaluation` stream (useChessStore.ts:923), skewing the in-game eval bar too.

I found no guard, precedence subtlety, type nuance, or unreachable-path argument that saves the code.

claim: `ensureReady()` awaits `readyok` with no timeout and no reject path, so a missing `readyok` hangs `setConfig`/`setPosition`/`newGame` forever instead of failing like `go()` does.
reasoning:
Confirmed from the code, though the reviewer's mechanism needs one correction. Two of the three refutations I tried are partially valid but do not close the hole:

(1) `failAllPending()` (chessEngineService.ts:605-608) DOES drain `readyWaiters` and is called from `worker.onerror` (line 249), so the narrow case "worker errors while a waiter is already pending" does not hang. That sub-case of the reviewer's story is wrong.

(2) `post()` throws when `this.worker === null`, and that throw inside the `new Promise` executor rejects the promise. But `worker` is only nulled in `terminate()`, and `terminate()`/`resetEngineService()` are called from nowhere in src/ (grep: only their own definitions). So this escape hatch is unreachable, and `postMessage` to a dead-but-non-null worker is a silent no-op.

The hole that survives: `failAllPending()` only drains waiters that exist at that instant. It sets no dead-engine flag and does not reset `isInitialized` — line 617 shows `isInitialized = false` happens only in `terminate()`. So after a single post-init `error` event the service is permanently stuck in "believes it is initialized, worker is dead", and every subsequent `ensureReady()` pushes a bare `resolve` (line 285) with no timer that nothing can ever settle.

Concrete reachable sequence: turn N `makeEngineMove` gets its `go()` rejected by `failAllPending` from `worker.onerror`; the `finally` at useChessStore.ts:948-950 sets `isEngineThinking: false`; `isEngineThinking` is in the dep array of the effect at GamePage.tsx:73-82, so `makeEngineMove()` re-fires immediately; this time `initialize()` short-circuits at line 231, `setConfig` posts setoptions into the void, and `ensureReady()` hangs forever. `await engine.setConfig(...)` at useChessStore.ts:920 never settles, so neither the `catch` nor the `finally` runs: `isEngineThinking` stays `true` permanently, no error is logged, the effect can never re-fire, and even `newGame()` (which resets `isEngineThinking` at line 896) just re-enters the same hang. Only a page reload recovers. The identical hang occurs on the FIRST `ensureReady()` if the worker wedges without firing `onerror`.

`go()` (lines 520-534) always arms a timer and the existing comment "Unblock anything waiting on `readyok` so callers don't hang forever" show this protection was intended and only half-implemented. The reviewer also missed a fourth unprotected call site, `setPositionFromMoves` at line 497. Their only overstatement is "no way for the player to move" — `isEngineThinking` gates only the thinking indicator and the auto-move effect, not human input; the game is nevertheless unplayable because the computer's move never arrives.

claim: makeMoveOnBoard hard-codes promotion to a queen and never receives the promotion piece the caller validated, so under-promotion requested over the socket is silently converted.
reasoning:
I could not refute it. The code confirms every mechanical detail. server/src/chess/moves.ts:201-208 declares makeMoveOnBoard with a fixed 6-parameter signature containing no promotion argument, and lines 238-244 unconditionally do `promotion = 'queen'; setPieceAt(board, to, { type: 'queen', color: piece.color });` for any pawn reaching the back rank. server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts:196 rejects a promotion move when `promotion` is missing, then lines 203-210 call makeMoveOnBoard with exactly six arguments, discarding the validated piece (a 7th argument would be a TS arity error, so this is not a misread). No guard compensates: I checked every `promotion` occurrence on the server — types.ts only declares types (PieceType is the full six-piece union, nothing narrows it to 'queen'), fen.ts:69-70 only appends the SAN suffix, and index.ts:146-158 forwards `promotion` verbatim into makeMove and broadcasts move/fen with no correction. So the board, move.promotion (line 230), move.san and room.currentFEN all report a queen for a requested knight.

The only genuine weakness in the claim is reachability, and it does not make the code correct. The client cannot currently emit the move: multiplayerService.makeMove (src/services/multiplayerService.ts:167) is called only by useChessStore.makeOnlineMove (src/store/useChessStore.ts:1065), and makeOnlineMove has zero callers in src/ — only its interface declaration at line 165. Both UI move paths (src/components/chess/Square.tsx:192 and handleSquareClick at useChessStore.ts:553) go to executeMove, which never forwards to the server, so online games presently transmit no moves at all. But the socket API is part of the declared shared contract (server/src/chess/types.ts:95 and src/chess/types.ts:151 both type makeMove as carrying promotion), the server validates that argument and then silently substitutes a queen for any caller, so the wrong behaviour is unconditional on the server. Verdict: defect real; the reviewer's 'boards diverge' narrative slightly overstates current reachability through the app UI.

Note for the fix: server/src/chess/fen.ts:70 builds the SAN suffix as promotion[0].toUpperCase(), which produces '=K' for 'knight'. That is latent only because promotion is always 'queen' today, so forwarding the real piece makes it live.

claim: `callWithCallback` invokes `(this.socket as any)[event](...)`, but socket.io-client's `Socket` has no per-event methods — every client→server action throws `TypeError`. It must be `this.socket.emit(event, ...args, cb)`.
reasoning: Refutation failed on every angle. (1) Code reads exactly as claimed: `(this.socket as any)[event](...args, cb)` at src/services/multiplayerService.ts:198. (2) socket.io-client 4.8.3 is installed and its `Socket` has no per-event methods — I walked the entire prototype chain in node (emit, emitWithAck, on, off, once, send, timeout, volatile, compress, connect, disconnect, ...; no createGame/makeMove) and grepped build/cjs plus @socket.io/component-emitter for `Proxy(` with zero hits, so there is no dynamic-method magic. (3) Empirically instantiated `io(url, {autoConnect:false})`: `typeof s.createGame === 'undefined'` and `s['createGame']({}, ()=>{})` throws `TypeError: s.createGame is not a function`. No own properties are added at construction either. (4) Nothing in src/ monkey-patches the socket (no Object.assign / prototype augmentation). (5) The path is reachable, not dead code: GamePage.tsx:165 renders <OnlineGameSetup />, whose handleCreateGame (OnlineGameSetup.tsx:29-45) awaits connectToServer() then createOnlineGame(), which hits useChessStore.ts:1012 -> multiplayerService.createGame -> callWithCallback. The line-193 guard only short-circuits when NOT connected, so once connect() resolves execution reaches line 198; a synchronous throw inside a Promise executor rejects the promise, and the component's catch renders the TypeError message. (6) The server (server/dist/index.js:48,64,91,108,148,158,167,175,201) registers `socket.on('createGame', (options, callback) => ...)` etc., confirming the correct wire form is emit-with-ack-callback-last. (7) ClientToServerEvents (src/chess/types.ts:147-157) only types the emit signature; it never adds methods to Socket, and the `as any` cast is why tsc still passes. Every client->server action (createGame/joinGame/leaveGame/makeMove/offerDraw/acceptDraw/declineDraw/resign/reconnectGame) funnels through this one line, so no online action can reach the server.

claim: A failed `initialize()` never terminates the worker it created, and a retry overwrites `this.worker`, so each retry leaks a live Worker that has started its own 112 MB wasm fetch.
reasoning:
Confirmed from the code. In src/services/chessEngineService.ts, both post-construction failure paths inside initialize() leave this.worker pointing at a live Worker: the onerror handler (line 247) calls failAllPending() + nulls initializationPromise + rejects, and failAllPending (line 590) only touches search/uciHandshake/readyWaiters — it never touches this.worker; the handshake timer (line 254) likewise only nulls uciHandshake and initializationPromise. Neither calls worker.terminate(), nulls the handlers, or resets isInitialized. Because isInitialized stays false and initializationPromise is null, the next initialize() falls through the two guards at lines 231-232 and assigns a brand-new Worker over the old reference at line 244, orphaning the previous one.

Re-entry is definitely reachable, and more aggressively than the reviewer claimed: src/pages/GamePage.tsx:72-82 lists isEngineThinking in the effect deps, and makeEngineMove (src/store/useChessStore.ts:908) swallows the error and sets isEngineThinking:false in its finally while currentTurn is still computerColor. The effect therefore immediately re-fires makeEngineMove -> engine.initialize(), giving an unbounded retry loop. On the onerror path (a 404 wasm fails in tens of ms) that spawns leaked workers as fast as the event loop allows; on the 180 s handshake-timeout path it leaks one live worker plus its in-flight multi-hundred-MB fetch every 3 minutes.

No external cleanup rescues this: a repo-wide grep shows terminate() and resetEngineService() are never called anywhere in src/ — the only hits are their own definitions at lines 611 and 637.

Refutations I tried and rejected: (a) "the orphan is GC'd once the reference is overwritten" — false, per the HTML spec a dedicated worker is kept alive by its owner Document, not by the JS Worker object reference, so it keeps running (and keeps its fetch alive) until terminate() or document destruction; (b) "post('uci') at line 269 throws first so no worker really starts" — impossible, this.worker was assigned on line 244; (c) the new Worker() constructor-throw path (lines 238-242) IS handled correctly, but that is a different path than the two alleged ones.

Additional confirmed consequence of the same omission: the orphaned worker's onmessage is still bound to this.handleLine, so a late uciok or bestmove from an abandoned worker resolves the *new* worker's handshake or the current search (setting isInitialized=true or resolving a search against stale output) — cross-talk layered on top of the memory/fetch leak.

Severity "fragile" is fair-to-generous; the unbounded retry loop makes it closer to a real resource-exhaustion bug.

claim: `makeEngineMove` installs an `onEvaluation` callback on the singleton engine and never removes it, so searches issued by the analysis store write into the game store's `engineEvaluation`.
reasoning:
Confirmed from the code; I could not find any guard that refutes it.

1. src/store/useChessStore.ts:923 installs `engine.onEvaluation(cb)` inside `makeEngineMove`. Grepping the whole `src/` tree, there is no `onEvaluation(null)` call anywhere — the only other occurrences of the name are the service's field and setter.

2. src/services/chessEngineService.ts:578 `onEvaluation` is a plain single-slot assignment (`this.onEvaluationCallback = callback`). None of `setConfig`, `setPosition`, `setPositionFromMoves`, `go`, `stop`, `newGame`, or `getBestMove` reset it. Even `terminate()` clears only `currentEvaluation`, `worker`, `isInitialized`, `initializationPromise` — not the callback.

3. `handleInfo` (chessEngineService.ts:337-353) invokes `this.onEvaluationCallback(evaluation)` unconditionally for every info line that carries a score or mate. It is NOT gated on `this.search` ownership (the `if (search)` block below it only populates the per-search MultiPV map). The single early return, `if (info.depth === undefined) return;`, is always satisfied by real search info lines.

4. The instance is shared. `useChessStore.ts:917` and `useAnalysisStore.ts:378/406/439/617` all call `getEngineService()` with no options, returning the same module-level singleton. `resetEngineService()` has zero callers in `src/`, so neither route changes nor new games recreate the instance — the leaked closure survives.

5. `useAnalysisStore.analyzeCurrentPosition` / `analyzeAllMoves` never register their own `onEvaluation`, so they do not even accidentally displace the game store's callback. The game store's closure over the (stable) Zustand `updateEngineEvaluation` action therefore fires for analysis-store searches and writes the analysed position's score into `useChessStore.engineEvaluation`. `analyzeAllMoves`'s per-move `engine.go({...})` loop does it repeatedly.

6. It is user-visible, not masked. `engineEvaluation` appears only three times in useChessStore.ts (type at 120, initial `null` at 220, setter at 953) — `resetGame` and `setGameMode` do not clear it. src/pages/GamePage.tsx:142 renders `<EvaluationBar />` and :145 `<EngineEvaluation className=... />` with no `evaluation` prop, so both take the `undefined -> storeEvaluation` fallback branch in EvaluationBar.tsx:24 / EngineEvaluation.tsx:26. Setting defaults (useSettingsStore.ts) are showCoordinates: true, showEvaluationBar: true, showEngineEvaluation: true, so both render gates are open by default. Because `makeEngineMove` ends with `updateEngineEvaluation(null)`, the steady-state on the game page is "bar hidden"; after an analysis run it becomes "bar visible showing an unrelated position's score", persisting until the next computer move. Routing is plain react-router with GamePage/AnalysisPage on separate routes and no shared mount, so nothing intervenes.

The reviewer's mechanism, trigger sequence, and observable outcome are all accurate. If anything the severity is understated (a hidden widget reappears with data sourced from a different store/position), though it is still cosmetic-only — no move legality, clock, or game-state corruption results.

claim: `isGameOver = gameStatus !== 'playing'` treats the 'idle' and 'check' statuses as game-over and swallows every click; every other component uses `!== 'playing' && !== 'idle'`.
reasoning: Could not refute; confirmed from source. ChessBoard.tsx:51 is literally `const isGameOver = gameStatus !== 'playing';` and line 55 short-circuits handleSquareClick before it reaches the store. GameStatus (src/chess/types.ts:57) includes 'idle' and 'check' as non-terminal states, and both are reachable: initialState.gameStatus is 'idle' (useChessStore.ts:189, no persist middleware, and newGame() at line 880 also sets 'idle'), and executeMove sets 'check' at line 428 whenever the opponent is in check but has legal moves. Nothing promotes 'idle' to 'playing' on mount — grep shows gameStatus:'playing' is only produced by loadFEN (line 701) and executeMove's status computation (line 402); GamePage.tsx has no start-game effect (its engine effect at line 73 already requires 'playing'). No alternate click path escapes the guard: Square.tsx wires onClick (218), onTouchEnd (219) and Enter/Space keydown (220) all through the passed-in onClick prop, and ChessPiece.tsx:27 is pointer-events-none with no handler, so piece clicks bubble to the same guarded div. Only drag bypasses it — handleDragStart calls selectPiece directly (Square.tsx:170) and handleDrop calls executeMove directly (Square.tsx:192), and those store actions guard only on the five terminal statuses (useChessStore.ts:239-247, 265-273), correctly permitting 'idle' and 'check'. Peer components agree the reviewer's semantics are the intended ones: BoardControls.tsx:38 and GameOverDialog.tsx:7 both use `!== 'playing' && !== 'idle'`. Result: click-to-move does nothing on a fresh load (first move only possible by drag), and stops working for both players whenever a check is on the board, including for the side that must get out of check.

claim: The draw-offer UI compares `drawOffer.offeredBy` against `currentTurn` instead of `myColor`, so in an online game both clients render the same branch and the receiving player is never shown Accept/Decline.
reasoning:
Confirmed from the code, not refutable. server/src/index.ts:192-200 broadcasts `gameState` to BOTH clients (io.to, which includes the sender) after a draw offer, and GameRoomManager.offerDraw (server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts:425-437) records {offeredBy: playerColor} with no turn validation. src/store/useChessStore.ts:1131 assigns `drawOffer: game.drawOffer` and 1119 assigns `currentTurn: game.turn`, so both clients hold identical values and every `drawOffer.offeredBy === currentTurn` test in BoardControls.tsx (lines 192, 194, 199, 201, 204, 205, 278, 305) evaluates identically on both clients. `myColor` exists (useChessStore.ts:114, set in createOnlineGame/joinOnlineGame, store is not persisted) but is never read in BoardControls.tsx. GamePage.tsx:155 renders BoardControls for online games, so the path is reachable.

Case A (white offers on white's turn — the natural flow): offeredBy === currentTurn on both clients, so the overlay at BoardControls.tsx:305 renders on BLACK's screen as well (it is not gated on showDrawConfirm, so it appears automatically and covers the UI). Its only button calls the purely local declineDraw() (useChessStore.ts:829-833 — no socket emit), and black's Draw button is disabled (line 192), so black can never accept or decline; the server's room.drawOffer is never cleared, so further offers fail with 'Draw already offered'.

Case B (offer while the opponent is to move — also reachable, no turn gate anywhere): both clients get the Accept affordance, so the offerer can accept its own offer. multiplayerService.callWithCallback rejects on success:false (multiplayerService.ts:199-204), the server returns 'Cannot accept own draw offer' (GameRoomManager.ts:445), and acceptDrawOffer (BoardControls.tsx:84-91) has no try/catch, so setShowDrawConfirm(false) never runs and the dialog is stuck open (identical for Decline, GameRoomManager.ts:462).

No alternative accept UI exists: drawOfferedBy is set at useChessStore.ts:992 but no component reads it. The one nuance is that the turn-based comparison is intentional-looking for local hotseat play, so the fix must branch on isOnlineGame rather than swapping currentTurn for myColor unconditionally.

claim: `makeMove` never clears `room.drawOffer`, so a pending offer survives every subsequent move and is re-broadcast in every `gameState`.
reasoning:
Confirmed. server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts makeMove (lines 179-325) updates castlingRights, enPassantTarget, halfmoveClock, fullmoveNumber, moveHistory, clocks, currentFEN, positionHistory, turn, gameStatus, result and updatedAt, but never assigns room.drawOffer. The only writes to drawOffer in the file are line 86 (init null), 433 (offerDraw), 449 (acceptDraw) and 464 (declineDraw) — none on the move path, and none in resign/handleTimeUp either. Because GameRoomInternal extends GameRoom, drawOffer is part of the object emitted at server/src/index.ts:159 (io.to(game.gameId).emit('gameState', game)) after every accepted move, and the client's applyServerGameState (src/store/useChessStore.ts:1131, `drawOffer: game.drawOffer`) installs it verbatim. moveMade is emitted before gameState on the same synchronous path, so the stale value lands last.

Both consequences are reachable. acceptDraw (line 439) checks only that room.drawOffer is truthy and offeredBy !== playerColor — no staleness check (the timestamp field written at line 433 is never read anywhere in src/ or server/src/) and not even a gameStatus guard — while BoardControls.tsx:204 renders the 'Accept' label whenever drawOffer.offeredBy !== currentTurn, so on any later black turn black gets a live Accept button for a 30-move-old white offer and can instantly draw a winning position. offerDraw (line 431) rejects on `if (room.drawOffer)` regardless of who offered, so white's later re-offer is permanently refused.

I attempted several refutations and all failed: there is no timestamp/staleness guard on either side; no client-side clearing of `drawOffer` on move (applyServerMove line 1152 clears the *separate* `drawOfferedBy` field, and BoardControls consumes `drawOffer`, not `drawOfferedBy`); socket.io preserves the moveMade-then-gameState ordering; and the server is authoritative so no client reset can survive.

Two framing errors in the reviewer's write-up, neither of which rescues the code: (1) drawOfferedBy and drawOffer are distinct store fields, so applyServerGameState does not literally "undo" the applyServerMove reset — instead `drawOffer` is simply never cleared anywhere; (2) the "no feedback at all" claim is overstated, since the Offer button is `disabled` when drawOffer.offeredBy === currentTurn (BoardControls.tsx:192), so white typically cannot even fire the doomed offerDraw. Separately, the leak is worse than reported: the full-screen blocking "Draw Offer Sent / Waiting for opponent to respond..." modal at BoardControls.tsx:305 is gated on drawOffer.offeredBy === currentTurn (currentTurn, not myColor), so one stale white offer pops that modal over BOTH players' boards on every white turn for the remainder of the game.

claim: The 1-second clock loop gates on `room.gameStatus === 'playing'` (and `handleTimeUp` re-checks the same at GameRoomManager.ts:389), so clock sync and flag detection stop entirely whenever a player is in check — the `isLiveStatus` helper written for exactly this is unused here.
reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not — every link in the chain checks out in the actual code.

1. `E:\open code\chess-app\server\src\index.ts:49` really is `if (room.gameStatus === 'playing' && room.clocks.isRunning)`. There is no `isLiveStatus` call, no second guard, and no second clock loop: `grep -rn "setInterval" server/src/` returns only the 5-minute cleanup (line 42) and this 1-second loop (line 47). `server/src/index.ts:58` is the only call site of `handleTimeUp` in the whole server.

2. `'check'` is a real reachable status, not a typo or dead branch. `server/src/chess/types.ts:4` declares `GameStatus = 'idle' | 'playing' | 'check' | ...`, and `GameRoomManager.makeMove` sets `room.gameStatus = 'check'` at `GameRoomManager.ts:307-308` for any checking move that is not mate. Checks are ordinary chess, so this is hit constantly in any real online game.

3. The clock is genuinely still live in that state. `switchClock` (`server/src/utils/clock.ts:82-89`) returns `isRunning: !isTimeUp` with `activeColor: nextColor`, and `stopClock` is only invoked on the terminal branches (checkmate/stalemate/draw/timeout/resign) — never on the `'check'` branch. So `room.clocks.isRunning === true` and the side to move is being charged, yet the loop's `=== 'playing'` test excludes the room. The second half of the `&&` cannot save it.

4. `handleTimeUp` re-gates identically at `GameRoomManager.ts:389`: `if (!room || room.gameStatus !== 'playing') return null;`. So even a caller that reached it during check would get `null`.

5. `getCurrentClocks` is non-mutating (`getCurrentClockState` -> `tickClock` returns a new object), so nothing else advances `room.clocks` in the background — skipping the loop skips all clock progress observable by clients.

6. The client side is as described. `useChessStore.ts:999-1001` is the only writer of `clock` for online games apart from `applyServerMove` (line 1151) / `applyServerGameState` (line 1133), which fire only on moves. The local ticker `tickClock` bails at `useChessStore.ts:760` (`if (!clock.isRunning || gameStatus !== 'playing') return;`), and `applyServerGameState` copies the server's `'check'` into client `gameStatus` (line 1121). `ClockDisplay.tsx:9-10` renders `clock.whiteMs`/`clock.blackMs` straight from the store, so with no `clockSync` and no local tick the displayed time is frozen — it is not recomputed from `lastTickMs` anywhere.

7. `getRunningGameIds()` (`GameRoomManager.ts:169-177`), which uses `isLiveStatus` correctly, is confirmed dead: a repo-wide grep for `getRunningGameIds` finds only its own definition. `isLiveStatus` is used only at lines 172 and 185.

Net effect, exactly as alleged: from the moment a checking move lands until the checked player moves, no `clockSync` is broadcast, both clients' clocks freeze, and if the checked side lets the flag fall while still in check, `handleTimeUp` is never called, so the game sits there indefinitely with a stale display. Note also that `makeMove` -> `isLiveStatus` (line 185) lets play continue from `'check'`, so the game is unambiguously meant to still be live in that state — the loop's gate is the outlier.

One adjacent finding worth flagging to the parent (not required to make this claim true): `handleTimeUp` calls `checkTimeUp(room.clocks)` on the *un-ticked* stored clock, whose `whiteMs`/`blackMs` were last written at the previous `switchClock`. Since nothing decrements `room.clocks` between moves, `checkTimeUp` will normally still see a positive value and return `null`, so simply widening the two status gates is necessary but not sufficient for the flag to actually be awarded — the ticked clock has to be committed to the room too.

claim: Nothing in the app ever calls `reconnectGame`; the store's `disconnect` handler only sets `opponentConnected: false`, so after socket.io's automatic reconnect the client is silently orphaned from its room.
reasoning: multiplayerService.reconnectGame() is defined at src/services/multiplayerService.ts:187 and the server handler at server/src/index.ts:251 is complete, but no code in the client ever calls it. The socket.io 'connect' event (fires on every reconnection) is not bridged through setupEventListeners and is not listened to in the store. After an auto-reconnect socket.io assigns a new socket.id; the server's playerToRoom still maps the dead id, so every subsequent action returns "Not in a game". opponentConnected is set false by playerLeft and is only restored by playerJoined, which is emitted only from joinGame and the reconnectGame server handler — neither of which runs after an auto-reconnect. The defect is fully reachable on any mid-game network blip.

I also ruled out indirect wiring: no `useChessStore.subscribe`, no effect watching `moveHistory` (the only `getState()` call sites are BoardControls.tsx:43,316 and settings reads). Reachability holds: `OnlineGameSetup` is gated on the same `isNewGameSetupOpen` flag as `NewGameSetup` and is mounted after it at equal z-50 (GamePage.tsx:163,165), so "New Game" surfaces the Create Online Game dialog; `handleCreateGame` runs `connectToServer()` + `createOnlineGame()`, setting `isOnlineGame: true` and `myColor` (useChessStore.ts:1014-1022) with a real room on the server. The server side is fully implemented (server/src/index.ts:146, server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts:179-197 including the 'Promotion required' branch), so it is dead code only because the client never emits. Server-status gating does not save it: a new room is 'idle' (GameRoomManager.ts:81) and ChessBoard.tsx:55 blocks clicks while status !== 'playing', but Square.tsx:192's drop path has no such gate and `executeMove` only rejects terminal statuses, so pieces can be dragged and both sides played locally while the server room sits at the initial FEN. The only overstatement in the claim is the two-player half of the scenario: `JoinGameModal` is unreachable because `isJoinGameOpen` is never set true (only `setIsJoinGameOpen(false)` at useChessStore.ts:1170 and inside the modal), which limits blast radius but does not change the defect.

claim: `reconnectPlayer` identifies the returning player by `id`/`socketId` — the very value that changes on reconnect — so it can never match a genuinely new connection.
reasoning:
I tried every refutation angle and all of them failed; the defect is independently confirmed from the code.

What I verified in `E:\open code\chess-app\server\src\game\GameRoomManager.ts`:

1. Identity is the ephemeral socket id, at every write site. `createGame` (lines 65-71) and `joinGame` (lines 113-119) both build `Player` as `{ id: socketId, ..., socketId }`. A repo-wide grep over `server/src` for assignments to `id` returns exactly two hits — `GameRoomManager.ts:66` and `:114` — both `id: socketId`. There is no other producer of `Player.id`, no uuid/token, no `socket.handshake.auth`, no client-supplied player id, and no `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` persistence of a player identity on the client. So `id` and `socketId` are always the *same old* socket id.

2. The match at lines 501-502 is against the *new* socket id. The sole caller is `E:\open code\chess-app\server\src\index.ts:253`, `gameRoomManager.reconnectPlayer(socket.id, gameId)` — it passes the freshly-connected socket's own id, never a client-supplied value, so there is no path by which the old id could reach the comparison.

3. The socket id really does change. `grep -rn connectionStateRecovery server/src src` returns nothing; the `new Server(...)` options at `index.ts:25-31` are `cors` only. socket.io 4.7.5 / socket.io-client 4.8.3 regenerate `socket.id` on every reconnection (and on page reload the client builds a brand-new socket anyway — `multiplayerService.connect()` calls `io(url, { reconnection: true, ... })` at `multiplayerService.ts:44-49`). So both disjuncts on 501 and 502 are false and control reaches line 514, `return { success: false, error: 'Not a participant in this game' }`. Exactly as claimed.

Refutations I attempted and ruled out:
- Precedence misread: no. Line 501 is `a?.id === socketId || (a?.socketId === socketId)` — the second disjunct is explicitly parenthesized, and `===` binds tighter than `||` regardless. Both operands compare to the same `socketId`.
- Nullability/type misunderstanding: no. `whitePlayer: Player | null` (`server/src/chess/types.ts:59-61`), `socketId?: string` (line 56); the optional chaining plus the `!` at 507/510 is sound. `undefined === socketId` is simply false for an empty slot, which is the intended behaviour.
- A guard elsewhere that rescues it: none. `leaveGame` (135-153) and the `disconnect` handler (`index.ts:233-247`) only flip `connected: false` while preserving the stale `id`/`socketId`; neither records any recoverable identity. `playerToRoom` is keyed by socket id too.
- Unreachable in practice: only partially, and it does not save the claim. The server handler `socket.on('reconnectGame', ...)` at `index.ts:251` is live and reachable by any socket client. It is true that the app's own client never invokes it — `multiplayerService.reconnectGame` is defined at `multiplayerService.ts:187-189` but a grep for `multiplayerService.` across `src/` shows no call site for it (only connect/createGame/joinGame/leaveGame/makeMove/offerDraw/acceptDraw/declineDraw/resign) — but the reviewer explicitly scoped around that ("even if the client were wired to call reconnectGame"), and this finding is precisely the blocker that would still remain after the wiring is added.

The decisive corroboration is an internal contradiction in the function itself: lines 507 and 510 write `socketId` back into the spread (`{ ...room.whitePlayer!, connected: true, socketId }`). That assignment is only meaningful if the incoming socket id *differs* from the stored one — i.e. the author assumed `Player.id` was a stable per-player token and `socketId` the volatile one. But `createGame`/`joinGame` set `id = socketId`, so the assumption never holds and the guard on 501-502 can only pass when the socket id has *not* changed, i.e. when no reconnection has occurred and the update is a no-op. The function works only in the case where it is not needed. Note also that `id` is never refreshed on reconnect, so it stays permanently stale.

claim: `applyGameEnd` maps every `reason` to `winner ? 'checkmate' : 'draw'`, so the statuses 'stalemate', 'timeout' and 'resigned' are never produced and the `reason` string is cast to `DrawReason` even when it is not one of its members.
reasoning:
Confirmed independently; refutation attempts failed.

1) src/store/useChessStore.ts:1156-1166 collapses every server reason to `winner ? 'checkmate' : 'draw'`, so 'stalemate', 'timeout' and 'resigned' — all valid members of GameStatus (src/chess/types.ts:57-65) — are unreachable from this action, and `reason as DrawReason` silently admits arbitrary strings (the assertion string -> literal union compiles, so tsc never flags it).

2) Emit order is exactly as alleged. server/src/index.ts (makeMove handler) emits 'moveMade', then 'gameState', then 'gameEnded' last inside `if (game.gameStatus !== 'playing')`. GameRoomManager.makeMove sets room.gameStatus = 'stalemate' (server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts:292) with result '1/2-1/2'. src/services/multiplayerService.ts:100-104 forwards socket events synchronously into emit() (line 150-152: plain forEach), so the client runs applyServerGameState (gameStatus 'stalemate') and then applyGameEnd, which overwrites gameStatus with 'draw' (winner is null for '1/2-1/2'). Nothing repairs it afterwards: the clockSync interval in server/src/index.ts only emits for rooms with gameStatus === 'playing', and makeOnlineMove ignores the ack payload.

3) The result is user-visible and durable. GameOverDialog (src/components/game/GameOverDialog.tsx:60-75) has a dedicated 'stalemate' branch ("Stalemate" / "Game drawn by stalemate") that becomes unreachable online; the 'draw' branch renders instead. The dialog is mounted unconditionally (src/pages/GamePage.tsx:161). Local play sets gameStatus 'stalemate' for the same position (useChessStore.ts:411-414), so online and local diverge for identical chess.

4) The drawReason half also holds. Resign/timeout/acceptDraw emit 'gameEnded' before 'gameState', so the bogus 'checkmate' status is transient (they are separate socket packets, so a render can occur between them), but drawReason durably keeps off-union strings: 'white resigned', 'Timeout: white flagged', 'Draw accepted', 'Checkmate! white wins'. Those are rendered verbatim wherever drawReason is shown (GameOverDialog.tsx:72 and MoveHistory.tsx:71 "DRAW — {drawReason}"), which is reachable e.g. for timeout-vs-insufficient-material where the server sets status 'draw' with reason 'Timeout: white flagged'.

Only mitigation: requires a running Socket.IO server and an online game, and stalemate is rare — that bounds frequency, not correctness. The online path is fully wired via OnlineGameSetup.tsx:37-38 and JoinGameModal.tsx:24-25.

claim: `leaveGame` only flips `connected: false` and never vacates the seat, so the room is permanently full and, given the socket-id-based `reconnectPlayer`, unjoinable by anyone afterwards.
reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every escape hatch I looked for is absent.

1. The code reads exactly as claimed. `E:\open code\chess-app\server\src\game\GameRoomManager.ts:135-153` (`leaveGame`) only does `room.whitePlayer = { ...room.whitePlayer, connected: false }` / the black equivalent, then `this.playerToRoom.delete(socketId)`. It never assigns `null` to either seat. No precedence or nullability misreading is involved; `whitePlayer`/`blackPlayer` are `Player | null` (server/src/chess/types.ts:61-62), so vacating would be type-legal and was simply not done.

2. There is no guard elsewhere. The socket handler at `E:\open code\chess-app\server\src\index.ts:128-143` only calls `manager.leaveGame`, `socket.leave`, and emits `playerLeft`; it does not touch the seats. The `disconnect` handler (index.ts:233-248) likewise only flips `connected: false`. `cleanup()` (GameRoomManager.ts:523-536) deletes a room only after 24h with both players disconnected. Nothing anywhere in server/src assigns null to a seat.

3. `joinGame` never consults `connected`. I grepped every use of `connected` in the server: it is read in exactly one place, `cleanup()` at lines 527-529. `joinGame`'s `if (room.whitePlayer && room.blackPlayer) return null;` (line 106) is purely occupancy-based, so a seat held by a disconnected/departed player permanently blocks joins. Server index.ts:100-102 turns that into the "Game not found or full" callback error the reviewer describes.

4. It is reachable in normal play, not a theoretical path. `leaveOnlineGame` is called from `src/components/game/BoardControls.tsx:109` (Rematch, rendered when `isGameFinished`) and from `src/components/game/GameOverDialog.tsx:103` and `:112`. `leaveOnlineGame` (src/store/useChessStore.ts:1048-1063) awaits `multiplayerService.leaveGame()` and resets the client to local mode, so the client genuinely abandons a room whose seat is still filled server-side. Re-entry via `JoinGameModal` -> `joinOnlineGame` -> `joinGame` then hits line 106.

5. The reconnect path does not rescue it. I grepped `reconnectGame` across the whole repo: it exists in `src/chess/types.ts:156`, `server/src/chess/types.ts:100`, `src/services/multiplayerService.ts:187-189`, and the server handler at index.ts:251 — but **no client code ever calls `multiplayerService.reconnectGame()`**. The reconnection feature is dead from the UI, so `joinGame` is the only reachable way back into a room. (One reviewer sub-claim is imprecise: immediately after Rematch, B's socket id has *not* changed, because `leaveGame` does not disconnect the socket, so `reconnectPlayer` would in principle succeed. That is moot given nothing calls it, and it does become true after any page reload. The conclusion is unaffected.)

Net effect, confirmed: after a post-game leave, the room is a zombie — the remaining player sees `opponentConnected: false` (playerLeft handler, useChessStore.ts:974-976) and waits forever, the vacated seat is unfillable by the leaver or any third player, and the room survives 24h of `cleanup()` polling. The `playerToRoom.delete(socketId)` in `leaveGame` shows the intent is a permanent departure, which makes leaving the seat occupied internally inconsistent.

Separate note, not part of this finding: `joinGame` also never checks `gameStatus`, so even if the seat were freed, a joiner would be dropped into a finished game with `gameStatus` forced back to `'playing'` (line 127). That needs handling too, but it is a distinct defect.

claim: `joinOnlineGame` derives `opponentName` as `whitePlayer?.name || blackPlayer?.name` without regard to which colour the joiner was assigned, so a joiner who gets white sees its own name as the opponent.
fix:
In src/store/useChessStore.ts at line 1038, select the player of the colour opposite to the joiner's assigned colour instead of falling back through white-then-black:

```ts
      opponentName:
        (response.color === 'white'
          ? response.game?.blackPlayer?.name
          : response.game?.whitePlayer?.name) || null,
```

`response.color` is the joiner's own colour and is already trusted on the adjacent line (`myColor: response.color`), so no extra plumbing is needed. This yields the creator's name in both the creator-as-white and creator-as-black cases.
reasoning:
I could not refute this; the defect is independently confirmed end-to-end.

Precedence/type angles fail: `?.` binds tighter than `||`, so line 1038 is `(game?.whitePlayer?.name) || (game?.blackPlayer?.name) || null`, and `whitePlayer: Player | null` (src/chess/types.ts:61) means the optional chain is legitimately nullable, not a misread type. The joiner's assigned colour (`response.color`, used on the adjacent line for `myColor`) is never consulted.

Reachability is confirmed and is in fact the default path: src/components/game/OnlineGameSetup.tsx:16 initialises `selectedColor` to `'random'`, and `'black'` is an explicit option. `GameRoomManager.createGame` sets `whitePlayer: color === 'white' ? player : null`, so a black/random-black creator leaves `whitePlayer === null` and `blackPlayer === creator`. `GameRoomManager.joinGame` (server/src/game/GameRoomManager.ts:109) then assigns the joiner white because `!room.whitePlayer`, and line 122 mutates `room.whitePlayer = player`, returning that same room object. server/src/index.ts:117-121 passes it straight back via `callback({ success: true, game, color })`, and `callWithCallback` (src/services/multiplayerService.ts:198-208) resolves the response verbatim with no field stripping. So `response.game.whitePlayer.name` genuinely is the joiner's own name, and `opponentName` becomes it.

My strongest refutation attempt — a later correction path — fails on all three candidates: (1) `applyServerGameState` (useChessStore.ts:1098-1135), invoked on the very next line, never writes `opponentName`; (2) the only other setter is the `playerJoined` handler at line 971, but the server emits it with `socket.to(game.gameId)` (server/src/index.ts:109), which excludes the joining socket, so the joiner never receives a `playerJoined` for the creator; (3) `gameState` broadcasts route into `applyServerGameState`, which again ignores `opponentName`. A grep for `opponentName` across src/ and server/ yields setters only at lines 971, 1019, 1038, 1057 — nothing rescues the value. ConnectionStatus.tsx:43 therefore renders the joiner's own name as the opponent for the whole game.

The reason the bug survived: when the creator picks white, the joiner gets black and `whitePlayer?.name` coincidentally IS the opponent, so the expression is correct by accident in that branch and wrong only in the creator-as-black branch (~50% of games under the default 'random' setting, 100% when Black is chosen explicitly).

claim: `worker.onerror` never resets `isInitialized` or terminates the worker, so an engine failure that happens after `uciok` leaves the service permanently wedged with no recovery path short of calling `terminate()`.
reasoning: Confirmed by direct reading. chessEngineService.ts:247-252 sets neither `isInitialized = false` nor tears down the worker, while `terminate()` (611-620) does all three. `isInitialized` is set true in the handshake resolve (262) and cleared only in `terminate()` (617), so after a post-`uciok` worker error `initialize()` short-circuits at line 231 and never spawns a replacement. `post()` (275-278) only throws when `this.worker` is null, and the dead worker is still retained, so commands are posted into the void. `ensureReady()` (280-288) awaits a promise with no timeout and no reject path, so `setConfig`/`setPosition` hang forever: `makeEngineMove` (useChessStore.ts:908-951) leaves `isEngineThinking: true` because its `finally` never runs, and GamePage.tsx:73-82 gates retries on `!isEngineThinking`, so the computer never moves again. `analyzeCurrentPosition` (useAnalysisStore.ts:377-402) hangs the same way with `isAnalyzing: true`. The `reject` at 251 is indeed a no-op after the init promise resolved. Grep over src/ shows nothing outside the service calls `terminate()`/`resetEngineService()`, `isReady()` is never called by any consumer, and there is no ErrorBoundary/window.onerror/unhandledrejection handler, so there is no recovery path. Reachability also checks out: in public/stockfish/stockfish-18-single.js the worker's `onmessage` dispatches through `i()` -> `o()` -> `c.ccall("command", ...)` with `async: false` and zero try/catch, so an Emscripten abort or wasm trap while applying `setoption name Hash value 64` on top of the 112,992,459-byte wasm image propagates uncaught out of `onmessage` and fires the parent's `worker.onerror` — exactly the alleged trigger, and `setConfig` (line 474) is the first thing sent after `uciok`. Refutation attempts failed: there is no second error listener, `post()` cannot throw with a retained worker, and only the pre-`uciok` path recovers correctly (it leaks the old worker but does re-spawn, since `isInitialized` is still false there).
